title: The Ghost Army: The Artists Who Fooled an Enemy With Rubber Tanks
description:
In 1944 the US Army's 23rd Headquarters Special Troops — about 1,100 men, many of them artists like Bill Blass and Ellsworth Kelly — used inflatable tanks, recorded sounds and fake radio traffic to stage about twenty deceptions, including Operation Viersen in March 1945. Much of the record was declassified in 1996; the unit received the Congressional Gold Medal in 2024.
Sources: National WWII Museum, Ghost Army Legacy Project, AP.
Animated with code, narration is synthetic.
